items.title: Leaving a Roth IRA to Your Kids? Why Dividend Stocks Make the 10-Year Rule Work for Them
items.summary: One stock in a six-pack of blue-chip dividend payers drives nearly two-fifths of the tax bill on an inherited portfolio, and it belongs somewhere else entirely. Your kids could pay for that mistake for decades.

items.title: Corporate Bonds vs. Dividend Stocks: Which Pays a Retiree More Reliably?
items.summary: Corporate bond yields just hit a 12-month high, yet that fat payout hides trade-offs in price risk, reinvestment, and taxes. For retirees weighing bonds against Procter & Gamble and Coca-Cola, the tax bill may decide the winner.

items.title: Turn $100,000 Into Lifetime Paychecks With These “Forever” Passive Income Dividend Stocks
items.summary: Four blue-chip dividend payers, from a drugmaker to an oil giant, promise income that grows while you never add a dollar. One of them yields more than double the others, and the reason behind that gap might surprise you.

items.title: If the Fed Hikes on Dec. 9, These 4 Dividend Stocks Are Built to Handle It
items.summary: Traders see a December rate rise as nearly certain, and it will separate dividends funded by surplus cash from those propped up by cheap debt. Which payouts, from pipelines to a Dividend King, look ready for the test?

items.title: Pre-holiday layoffs hit over 7,600 workers in trucking, logistics, manufacturing
items.summary: Trucking contractors, logistics providers and manufacturers are cutting jobs across the U.S. heading into the holiday season. The post Pre-holiday layoffs hit over 7,600 workers in trucking, logistics, manufacturing appeared first on FreightWaves.

items.title: 3 Top Dividend Stocks to Buy and Hold for Decades
items.summary: Looking beyond high yields, PG, KO, and MCD offer the potential for decades of dividend income and long-term returns.

items.title: Will Procter & Gamble's Restructuring Plan Sharpen Its Cost Base?
items.summary: PG is accelerating restructuring and productivity initiatives to sharpen its cost base, but rising input costs could limit near-term profitability gains.

items.title: Anthropic falls below IPO price as Nvidia gives back gains
items.summary: In this edition of Sozzi Unleashed: At The Close, Brian Sozzi sorts through "reality trading" as Nvidia slides nearly 7% after Monday's 31% surge and Anthropic falls below its $83 IPO price less than a week after the biggest offering in history. GCG Advisory Partners' Bill Gunderson makes the case that Nvidia is the cheapest growth stock in the market at nine times forward earnings and names Nvidia and Eli Lilly as his top picks for 2027. Brian breaks down Dell's blowout quarter and $132 billion AI backlog, and HPE CEO Antonio Neri joins to explain the company's raised outlook, why it refuses to finance neoclouds, and whether server margins have peaked. Brian closes by arguing the AI trade is reaching consumers' wallets, pointing to Best Buy's strongest comparable sales growth in five years.
